 Oral Judgment
This appeal is preferred by the claimants, seeking enhancement of compensation and also as to the
liability, assailing the judgment and award dated 03.03.2020 in Mvc No.226/2016 on the file of the
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Raichur (for short 'the Tribunal', partly allowing the claim
petition and awarding compensation.

2.  It is the case of the claimants that, on 19.03.2016 at about 7.00 p.m., the son of the claimants - Veerabhadrayyaswamy was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-37/R-6961 on Sindhanur-Raichur Road near English Medium School, Araginamara Camp, Sindhanur Taluk and respondent No.1 had parked the lorry bearing No.KA-36-4716 in the middle of the road and due to the darkness, the rider of the motorcycle - deceased could not see the said lorry and has hit the lorry, due to which he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, the claimants have preferred MVC No.226/2016 before the Tribunal, seeking compensation.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR 3.
The claim petition was contested by the respondents.
4. In order to establish their case, the claimants have examined one witness as PW.1 and got marked 42 documents as Exs.P1 to P42.

On the other hand, the respondents have examined 02 witnesses as RWs.1 and 2 and got marked 07 documents as Exs.R1 to R7.
5.
The Tribunal, after considering the material on record, by judgment and award dated 03.03.2020 has determined total compensation at Rs.16,45,192/-.

However, the Tribunal has held the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased towards the alleged accident to an extent of 50%
and fastened the remaining 50% liability on respondent No.3-Insurace Company and thereby,
awarded only 50% of compensation i.e., Rs.8,22,596/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants have preferred by this appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR 6.

I have heard Smt. Patil Shantabai Subhash, learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri Sudrashan M., learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3-Insurance Company.
7.

It is argued by the learned counsel appearing for the appellants that, the Tribunal has erred in holding the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, which requires to be set right in this appeal.

It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the appellants that, the award of Sri Adayyaswamy And Anr vs Syed Najeemuddin And Others on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85849179/
3 compensation is meager, which requires to be enhanced.

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3-Insurance Company sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

9. Having taken note of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and also taking into account Ex.P2-spot panchanama, would make it clear that, the rider of the motorcycle-deceased has also NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR contributed towards the alleged accident and hit the lorry in question from behind.
In that view of the matter, the finding recorded by the Tribunal on issue No.1 by taking into account Ex.P2 is just and proper, which does not call for any interference in this appeal.
10. Insofar as enhancement of compensation is concerned, perusal of the records would indicate that, the deceased was a MBA Graduate and Bachelor.
In that view of the matter, as the employer has been examined as RW.2, the Salary Certificate has to be considered and the income of the deceased is to be considered at Rs.12,000/- per month.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Tribunal has rightly added 40% towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the multiplier of '17' and the deductions towards personal expenses of the deceased at 50% considered by the Tribunal is also just and proper.

Thus, the appellants are entitled for Rs.17,13,600/-
NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR towards loss of dependency (Rs.12,000 + 40% x 12 x 17 x 1/2)
11.

As per the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the dictum of Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, and United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others reported in (2020) 9 SCC 644, the appellants being the parents of the deceased are entitled for Rs.40,000/-
towards filial consortium.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi Supra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Further, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rasmita Biswal and others NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2022) 2 SCCC 767, there shall be an escalation of 10% for every three years.

entities.text: Rasmita Biswal and others NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and another reported in (2022) 2 SCCC 767
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, since the accident in question had occurred in the year 2016, the appellants herein are entitled for 30% escalation on the conventional heads i.e., loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

14. Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed as under:
Loss of dependency Rs.17,13,600 Loss of consortium Rs.80,000/-
Conventional heads Rs.30,000/-

Thus, the appellants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.18,56,600/-.
15.

Since the deceased has also contributed to the accident to an extent of 50%, the appellants are entitled for only 50% of the total compensation i.e., Rs.9,28,300/-
NC: 2026:KHC-K:957 HC-KAR with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

16. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellants/claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.9,28,300/- along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
(iii) Respondent No.3-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
